title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 5-7). X is a complete algebraic curve over Q-bar, D = ΣD_i a reduced divisor indexed by a finite set I, and X' = X − D the open curve. The marginal note on p.7 ('il faut dire X = X' − I'), with the roles of X and X' swapped, shows Grothendieck himself flags the notation. π_1(X') is the geometric profinite fundamental group of the open curve. Γ = Gal(Q-bar/Q). G_{X'} is the group of semi-linear automorphisms of X' (pairs (u,σ) with σ ∈ Γ and u a σ-linear automorphism), with a map G_{X'} → Γ whose image contains Γ' (the field-of-moduli situation). E_{X'} is the extension 1 → π_1(X') → E_{X'} → G_{X'} → 1 (14). This gives an outer action of G_{X'} on π_1(X'), and sections φ_ξ: Γ' → E_{X'} attached to rational points ξ (15).

Data from the previous page. G_{X'} permutes the punctures, G_{X'} → S_I (16). Kummer theory gives, for each i ∈ I, an outer homomorphism φ_i: T(Q-bar) = Ẑ(1) = lim μ_n → π_1(X') (17). Its image is the conjugacy class of inertia subgroups at D_i, with a canonical generator. G_{X'} acts on Ẑ(1) through Γ via the cyclotomic character χ: Γ → Ẑ* = Aut(Ẑ(1)) (18).

This page, first statement. The outer action of G_{X'} on π_1(X') respects the family (φ_i), the 'Kummer structures', once one accounts for the twisting by (16) on I and (18) on T. So the outer representation factors through (19):

G_{X'} → Autext(π_1(X'), T, (φ_i)).

This target is the group of 'cuspidal' (inertia-preserving) semi-linear outer automorphisms. It is the profinite counterpart of the extended mapping class group of a punctured surface, with the cyclotomic twist built in.

This page, second construction. Grothendieck refines from outer to actual homomorphisms. Let X̃' be the normalization of the complete curve X in the universal profinite étale cover of X'. This gives a pro-object X̃'^ → X, ramified exactly over D. Let X̃'(I) be the inverse image of the points of D (the 'cusps' of the universal cover). It maps to I (20). E_{X'} acts on X̃'(I) compatibly with the action of G_{X'} on I and with (20). For each i, the fibre X̃'(i) is a homogeneous space under π_1(X') (21); stabilizers are the inertia subgroups.

On p.7 this yields maps X̃'(i) → Hom(T, π_1(X')) (22) and a global E_{X'}-equivariant map X̃'(I) → Hom(T, π_1(X')) (23), equivariance also involving the action on T via Γ. This lifts the outer classes φ_i to genuine homomorphisms indexed by cusps. The purpose is a purely group-theoretic, profinite description of a punctured curve together with its arithmetic (Galois) and automorphism data. This is the anabelian/Teichmüller 'paradigm' viewpoint of Esquisse and Longue Marche: the curve is encoded by (π_1, T, Kummer structures, E-action).
errors: Notational inconsistency between X and X' (complete vs open curve). The text says 'normalisé de X dans l'extension définie par X'' and uses π_1(X') with nontrivial inertia, so X' must be the open curve. Grothendieck's own marginal note on the next page flags the need to state the relation between X, X' and I.

In (21) the group acting should be π_1(X') (open curve), not π_1 of the normalized pro-cover. The stabilizers are inertia subgroups isomorphic to Ẑ(1) only in the generic (hyperbolic, or at least non-degenerate) case. For small cases, such as P^1 minus one or two points, inertia is trivial or the whole abelian group, and the 'homogeneous space' statement degenerates.

(19) is stated without justification. It is standard: a semi-linear automorphism maps local monodromy at D_i to local monodromy at its image, with the cyclotomic twist. The twisted compatibility is only sketched ('compte tenu des gradations').

ideas.what: Outer Galois/automorphism representation on the profinite π_1 of a punctured curve preserves the inertia classes (Kummer structures) up to permutation of cusps and cyclotomic twist, (19).
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore from SGA1 tame ramification; systematized by Ihara, Belyi, Nakamura, Matsumoto (1980s-90s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche discuss outer Galois actions respecting inertia ('lacets' at punctures). The packaging as 'structures Kummériennes' is not, to my knowledge, published.

ideas.what: Extension E_{X'} of the semi-linear automorphism group G_{X'} by π_1(X'), with sections from rational points (field-of-moduli setting).
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group extension of a curve with automorphisms; field of moduli vs field of definition via π_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 exact sequence); Dèbes–Douai and others for field-of-moduli use
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (exact homotopy sequence); Longue Marche, letter to Faltings (sections conjecture context)

ideas.what: Normalizing the complete curve in the universal profinite cover of the open curve to obtain the profinite set of cusps X̃'(I). It is fibred over I, with π_1-homogeneous fibres, carries an E-action, and has an equivariant map to Hom(Ẑ(1), π_1) lifting outer inertia classes to genuine homomorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: cusps of the universal pro-étale cover; cuspidal inertia/decomposition subgroups
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Nakamura, Mochizuki, Tamagawa in anabelian geometry)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse (profinite surface groups with 'lacets'). The explicit construction on this page is unpublished.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, careful early formulation, around 1980, of the cuspidal ('Kummer structure') outer Galois representation and of the profinite set of cusps of the universal cover. It shows Grothendieck setting up the inertia-preserving framework later standard in anabelian geometry and Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. However, all content is now standard and essentially routine for specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'pts [-quelconques-] {+multiples[?]+}': the overwritten word is uncertain; the sense is simply the points lying over the support of D = ΣD_i.
In the marginal note to (21), the image reads 'C'est un espace homogène sous π_1(X̃')'. Mathematically this should be π_1(X') (the open curve).
In (19) the second argument is written over a correction but is T(Q̄), as on the previous page.
'le normalisé de X dans l'extension définie par X'': the image appears to read 𝔛 (not 𝔛') after 'normalisé de'. This is consistent with X being the complete curve and X' the open one.
